question: An investigator is studying muscle tissue in high-performance athletes. He obtains blood samples from athletes before and after a workout session consisting of short, fast sprints. Which of the following findings is most likely upon evaluation of blood obtained after the workout session?
analysis: During high-intensity exercise like short, fast sprints, the muscles rely on anaerobic metabolism to produce energy. This leads to an increased concentration of lactate due to the breakdown of glucose. Additionally, there is an accumulation of H+ ions causing a decrease in pH. Insulin levels typically decrease during exercise to allow for the release of glucose into the bloodstream for energy production. ATP levels may increase to meet the energy demands of the muscles. NADH levels may decrease temporarily as it is utilized in the electron transport chain for ATP production.
